item.title: 'Stranger Things' Fans Can't Ignore Eleven's 'Mewing Face' In The Newest Season Of The Hit Netflix Series
item.description: Eleven Mewing Face or Eleven Serving Face, also known as Chad Face Eleven refers to memes about the appearance of Millie Bobby Brown as Eleven's face in Stranger Things season five, implying that she got plastic surgery before filming. Some of the memes compare Eleven's face to the typical Chad face and joke that she's been mewing. The memes were popularized in December 2025 surrounding the Christmas day release of season five, volume two.

item.title: What Is The 'Eleven Face Meme?' The Viral 'Stranger Things 5' Memes About Eleven's Mewing Face Explained
item.description: The fifth and final season of 'Stranger Things' is taking over social media, but fans can't help noticing a change in Eleven's face. Here's what you need to know.

item.title: 'It's A Surprise' Kid's Adorable Viral Video Becomes A Big Green Screen Meme On TikTok
item.description: "Come Over, It's a Surpise" Kid is a series of memes, including green screen edits, based on a viral video of a child, TikToker @mralexandes, telling his mother to "come over" and then saying "it's a surprise" when asked where he's going to bring her. The video was posted to TikTok in late December 2025 and became the subject of memes over the following days, including accuracy reenactments and edits that apply captions about luring someone somewhere.

item.title: Fan Favorite Moment From 'Phoenix Wright: Ace Attorney' Is An Annual Holiday Season Tradition
item.description: "Almost Christmas" Means It Wasn't Christmas is a line spoken by the character Phoenix Wright in the visual novel, Phoenix Wright: Ace Attorney, originally released in mid-October 2001. The catchphrase and scene later became a meme among the video game's fandom and are traditionally posted annually in December, most commonly on December 24th, just before Christmas Day. Variations of the meme include fan art depictions, redraws, exploitables and more.

item.title: Police Bodycam Footage Released, Offering More Context To The Viral 'Cinnabon Girl' Video
item.description: The Racist Cinnabon Employee Controversy or "Cinnabon Girl" Crystal Wilsey refers to discourse surrounding a viral video of an employee at a Cinnabon in Wisconsin, Crystal Wilsey, calling two Somalian Muslim customers the n-word and making obscene gestures at them while on the job. In the video, uploaded by TikTokers @skylight7373 and @dailypaypis in early December 2025, she admits to being racist, calls them the n-word several times, flips them off.
